passages.text: After Jesus had spoken these words, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron Valley, where they entered a garden.
passages.sermon:
Jesus finished speaking these words.
He left with His disciples.
They crossed the Kidron Valley.
There was a garden on the other side.
Jesus entered the garden.
His disciples entered the garden with Him.
passages.original: Ταῦτα εἰπὼν Ἰησοῦς ἐξῆλθεν σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ πέραν τοῦ χειμάρρου τοῦ Κέδρων ὅπου ἦν κῆπος εἰς ὃν εἰσῆλθεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Now Judas His betrayer also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with His disciples.
passages.sermon: Judas was the one who would betray Jesus.\r\nJudas knew the place.\r\nJesus had often met there with His disciples.
passages.original: ᾔδει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν τὸν τόπον ὅτι πολλάκις συνήχθη Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖ μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. They arrived at the garden carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.
passages.sermon:
Judas was the betrayer of Jesus.
Judas took a group of soldiers with him.
Judas also took officers from the chief priests.
Judas also took officers from the Pharisees.
Judas and the group went to the garden.
They carried lanterns.
They carried torches.
They carried weapons.
passages.original: ὁ οὖν Ἰούδας λαβὼν τὴν σπεῖραν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων ὑπηρέτας ἔρχεται ἐκεῖ μετὰ φανῶν καὶ λαμπάδων καὶ ὅπλων

passages.text: Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon Him, stepped forward and asked them, “Whom are you seeking?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew everything that would happen to Him.
He stepped forward.
He spoke to them.
He asked, “Whom are you seeking?”
passages.original: Ἰησοῦς οὖν εἰδὼς πάντα τὰ ἐρχόμενα ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἐξῆλθεν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τίνα ζητεῖτε

passages.text: “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered. Jesus said, “I am He.” And Judas His betrayer was standing there with them.
passages.sermon:
A group of people came to arrest Jesus.
Judas was with them.
Judas was the one who would betray Jesus.
The group answered Jesus.
They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “I am He.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον Λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἐγώ εἰμι Εἱστήκει δὲ καὶ Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν

passages.text: When Jesus said, “I am He,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the group that came to arrest Him.
Jesus said to them, “I am He.”
The group heard Jesus say, “I am He.”
They moved backward.
They fell to the ground.
passages.original: ὡς οὖν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγώ εἰμι ἀπῆλθον εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ ἔπεσαν χαμαί

passages.text: So He asked them again, “Whom are you seeking?” “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the group.
He spoke to them again.
He asked, “Whom are you seeking?”
They answered Him.
They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
passages.original: Πάλιν οὖν ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτούς Τίνα ζητεῖτε Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον

passages.text: “I told you that I am He,” Jesus replied. “So if you are looking for Me, let these men go.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the crowd.\r\nJesus said, "I told you that I am He."\r\nJesus said, "If you are looking for Me, let these men go."
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι εἰ οὖν ἐμὲ ζητεῖτε ἄφετε τούτους ὑπάγειν

passages.text: This was to fulfill the word He had spoken: “I have not lost one of those You have given Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke a word before this moment.
He said, “I have not lost one of those You have given Me.”
This event happened to fulfill that word.
Jesus kept safe all the people God gave Him.
He did not lose any of them.
passages.original: ἵνα πληρωθῇ ὁ λόγος ὃν εἶπεν ὅτι Οὓς δέδωκάς μοι οὐκ ἀπώλεσα ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐδένα

passages.text: Then Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Simon Peter had a sword.
Simon Peter drew his sword.
Simon Peter struck the servant of the high priest.
Simon Peter cut off the servant’s right ear.
The servant’s name was Malchus.
passages.original: Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος ἔχων μάχαιραν εἵλκυσεν αὐτὴν καὶ ἔπαισεν τὸν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως δοῦλον καὶ ἀπέκοψεν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὠτάριον τὸ δεξιόν ἦν δὲ ὄνομα τῷ δούλῳ Μάλχος

passages.text: “Put your sword back in its sheath!” Jesus said to Peter. “Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus said, “Put your sword away.”
Jesus said, “The Father has given Me a cup to drink.”
Jesus said, “I must drink this cup.”
passages.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ Βάλε τὴν μάχαιραν εἰς τὴν θήκην τὸ ποτήριον ὃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ Πατήρ οὐ μὴ πίω αὐτό

passages.text: Then the band of soldiers, with its commander and the officers of the Jews, arrested Jesus and bound Him.
passages.sermon:
A group of soldiers came.
Their commander was with them.
The officers of the Jews were also there.
They arrested Jesus.
They tied Him up.
passages.original: Ἡ οὖν σπεῖρα καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται τῶν Ἰουδαίων συνέλαβον τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἔδησαν αὐτὸν

passages.text: They brought Him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers and officers took Jesus.
They brought Jesus to Annas first.
Annas was the father-in-law of Caiaphas.
Caiaphas was the high priest that year.
passages.original: καὶ ἤγαγον πρὸς Ἅνναν πρῶτον ἦν γὰρ πενθερὸς τοῦ Καϊάφα ὃς ἦν ἀρχιερεὺς τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ ἐκείνου

passages.text: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it would be better if one man died for the people.
passages.sermon: Caiaphas was the high priest that year.\r\nCaiaphas had given advice to the Jews.\r\nHe said it would be better if one man died for the people.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ Καϊάφας ὁ συμβουλεύσας τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι συμφέρει ἕνα ἄνθρωπον ἀποθανεῖν ὑπὲρ τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: Now Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus. Since that disciple was known to the high priest, he also went with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter followed Jesus.
Another disciple also followed Jesus.
This other disciple was known to the high priest.
This disciple went with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
passages.original: Ἠκολούθει δὲ τῷ Ἰησοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ ἄλλος μαθητής ὁ δὲ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ἦν γνωστὸς τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ καὶ συνεισῆλθεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τοῦ ἀρχιερέως

passages.text: But Peter stood outside at the door. Then the disciple who was known to the high priest went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
passages.sermon:
Peter stood outside at the door.
Another disciple was there.
This other disciple knew the high priest.
He went out to the doorkeeper.
He spoke to the doorkeeper.
He brought Peter inside.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος εἱστήκει πρὸς τῇ θύρᾳ ἔξω ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ὁ ἄλλος ὁ γνωστὸς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θυρωρῷ καὶ εἰσήγαγεν τὸν Πέτρον

passages.text: At this, the servant girl watching the door said to Peter, “Aren’t you also one of this man’s disciples?” “I am not,” he answered.
passages.sermon:
A servant girl stood at the door.
She watched who entered.
She spoke to Peter.
She asked Peter, “Are you also one of this man’s disciples?”
Peter answered her.
He said, “I am not.”
passages.original: Λέγει οὖν τῷ Πέτρῳ ἡ παιδίσκη ἡ θυρωρός Μὴ καὶ σὺ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν εἶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου Λέγει ἐκεῖνος Οὐκ εἰμί

passages.text: Because it was cold, the servants and officers were standing around a charcoal fire they had made to keep warm. And Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
passages.sermon:
It was cold.
The servants stood there.
The officers stood there too.
They had made a charcoal fire.
They stood around the fire.
They warmed themselves.
Peter was with them.
Peter stood with them.
Peter was warming himself.
passages.original: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι καὶ οἱ ὑπηρέται ἀνθρακιὰν πεποιηκότες ὅτι ψῦχος ἦν καὶ ἐθερμαίνοντο ἦν δὲ καὶ ὁ Πέτρος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἑστὼς καὶ θερμαινόμενος

passages.text: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and His teaching.
passages.sermon:
The high priest was present.
The high priest questioned Jesus.
He asked Jesus about His disciples.
He asked Jesus about His teaching.
passages.original: Ὁ οὖν ἀρχιερεὺς ἠρώτησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν περὶ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “I have spoken openly to the world,” Jesus answered. “I always taught in the synagogues and at the temple, where all the Jews come together. I said nothing in secret.
passages.sermon:
Jesus answered the high priest.
Jesus spoke openly to everyone in the world.
Jesus always taught in the synagogues.
Jesus also taught in the temple.
All the Jews gather in these places.
Jesus never spoke in secret.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγὼ παρρησίᾳ λελάληκα τῷ κόσμῳ ἐγὼ πάντοτε ἐδίδαξα ἐν συναγωγῇ καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ὅπου πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι συνέρχονται καὶ ἐν κρυπτῷ ἐλάλησα οὐδέν

passages.text: Why are you asking Me? Ask those who heard My message. Surely they know what I said.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest.
The high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and His teaching.
Jesus said, "Why are you asking Me?"
Jesus told the high priest to ask the people who heard Him speak.
Jesus said, "Ask those who heard My message."
Jesus said, "They know what I said."
The people who listened to Jesus know His words.
passages.original: τί με ἐρωτᾷς ἐρώτησον τοὺς ἀκηκοότας τί ἐλάλησα αὐτοῖς ἴδε οὗτοι οἴδασιν ἃ εἶπον ἐγώ

passages.text: When Jesus had said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped Him in the face and said, “Is this how You answer the high priest?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest.
He spoke openly and answered questions.
An officer stood nearby.
This officer heard Jesus speak.
The officer slapped Jesus in the face.
The officer said, “Is this how you answer the high priest?”
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ εἰπόντος εἷς παρεστηκὼς τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἔδωκεν ῥάπισμα τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἰπών Οὕτως ἀποκρίνῃ τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ

passages.text: Jesus replied, “If I said something wrong, testify as to what was wrong. But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the high priest’s officer.
The officer had just struck Jesus in the face.
Jesus spoke to the officer.
Jesus said, “If I spoke wrongly, tell me what was wrong.”
Jesus also said, “If I spoke rightly, why do you hit me?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς Εἰ κακῶς ἐλάλησα μαρτύρησον περὶ τοῦ κακοῦ εἰ δὲ καλῶς τί με δέρεις

passages.text: Then Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
passages.sermon:
Annas was a Jewish leader.
Annas held Jesus as a prisoner.
Annas kept Jesus tied up.
Annas sent Jesus to Caiaphas.
Caiaphas was the high priest.
passages.original: Ἀπέστειλεν οὖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἅννας δεδεμένον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα

passages.text: Simon Peter was still standing and warming himself. So they asked him, “Aren’t you also one of His disciples?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter stood nearby.
He warmed himself by the fire.
Some people spoke to Simon Peter.
They asked him a question.
They said, “Are you also one of Jesus’ disciples?”
Simon Peter answered them.
He denied being a disciple.
He said, “I am not.”
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος ἑστὼς καὶ θερμαινόμενος εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ σὺ ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶ Ἠρνήσατο ἐκεῖνος καὶ εἶπεν Οὐκ εἰμί

passages.text: One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, asked, “Didn’t I see you with Him in the garden?”
passages.sermon:
One servant of the high priest spoke.
This servant was a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off.
He asked Peter a question.
He said, “Didn’t I see you with Jesus in the garden?”
passages.original: Λέγει εἷς ἐκ τῶν δούλων τοῦ ἀρχιερέως συγγενὴς ὢν οὗ ἀπέκοψεν Πέτρος τὸ ὠτίον Οὐκ ἐγώ σε εἶδον ἐν τῷ κήπῳ μετ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Peter denied it once more, and immediately a rooster crowed.
passages.sermon: Peter stood there.\r\nPeter denied it again.\r\nA rooster crowed right away.
passages.original: Πάλιν οὖν ἠρνήσατο Πέτρος καὶ εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν

passages.text: Then they led Jesus away from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. By now it was early morning, and the Jews did not enter the Praetorium, to avoid being defiled and unable to eat the Passover.
passages.sermon:
The people took Jesus away from Caiaphas.
They led Jesus into the Praetorium.
It was early in the morning.
The Jews did not go into the Praetorium.
They did not enter because they did not want to be defiled.
They wanted to eat the Passover.
passages.original: Ἄγουσιν οὖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ Καϊάφα εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον ἦν δὲ πρωΐ καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐκ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον ἵνα μὴ μιανθῶσιν ἀλλὰ φάγωσιν τὸ πάσχα

passages.text: So Pilate went out to them and asked, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate went outside to meet the Jewish leaders.
Pilate spoke to them.
Pilate asked a question.
He said, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
passages.original: Ἐξῆλθεν οὖν ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἔξω πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ φησίν Τίνα κατηγορίαν φέρετε κατὰ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου

passages.text: “If He were not a criminal,” they replied, “we would not have handed Him over to you.”
passages.sermon: The Jewish leaders answered Pilate.\r\nThey said, “This man has done evil.”\r\n“If he were not doing wrong, we would not have brought him to you.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Εἰ μὴ ἦν οὗτος κακὸν ποιῶν οὐκ ἄν σοι παρεδώκαμεν αὐτόν

passages.text: “You take Him and judge Him by your own law,” Pilate told them. “We are not permitted to execute anyone,” the Jews replied.
passages.sermon:
Pilate spoke to the Jewish leaders.
He said, “You take Him.”
He said, “Judge Him by your own law.”
The Jewish leaders answered Pilate.
They said, “We are not allowed to put anyone to death.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος Λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑμῶν κρίνατε αὐτόν Εἶπον αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Ἡμῖν οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἀποκτεῖναι οὐδένα

passages.text: This was to fulfill the word that Jesus had spoken to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
passages.sermon: Jesus had spoken about His death.\r\nHe had said what kind of death He would die.\r\nThese events happened to fulfill His words.
passages.original: ἵνα ὁ λόγος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πληρωθῇ ὃν εἶπεν σημαίνων ποίῳ θανάτῳ ἤμελλεν ἀποθνήσκειν

passages.text: Pilate went back into the Praetorium, summoned Jesus, and asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate went back into the Praetorium.
Pilate called for Jesus.
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate asked Jesus a question.
Pilate said, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
passages.original: Εἰσῆλθεν οὖν πάλιν εἰς τὸ πραιτώριον ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἐφώνησεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: “Are you saying this on your own,” Jesus asked, “or did others tell you about Me?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Pilate.
Jesus asked Pilate a question.
Jesus said, “Are you saying this on your own?”
Jesus also asked, “Or did others tell you about Me?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἀπὸ σεαυτοῦ σὺ τοῦτο λέγεις ἢ ἄλλοι εἶπόν σοι περὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: “Am I a Jew?” Pilate replied. “Your own people and chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate said, “Am I a Jew?”
Pilate said, “Your own people handed you over to me.”
Pilate said, “The chief priests gave you to me.”
Pilate asked, “What have you done?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος Μήτι ἐγὼ Ἰουδαῖός εἰμι τὸ ἔθνος τὸ σὸν καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς παρέδωκάν σε ἐμοί τί ἐποίησας

passages.text: Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My kingdom is not of this realm.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Pilate.
Jesus said, “My kingdom does not come from this world.
If my kingdom came from this world, my servants would fight for me.
They would stop me from being handed over to the Jewish leaders.
But my kingdom is not from here.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς Ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου εἰ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου τούτου ἦν ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμή οἱ ὑπηρέται ἄν οἱ ἐμοὶ ἠγωνίζοντο ἵνα μὴ παραδοθῶ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις νῦν δὲ ἡ βασιλεία ἡ ἐμὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντεῦθεν

passages.text: “Then You are a king!” Pilate said. “You say that I am a king,” Jesus answered. “For this reason I was born and have come into the world, to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to My voice.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate asked, “So, you are a king?”
Jesus answered Pilate.
Jesus said, “You say that I am a king.”
Jesus said, “I was born for this reason.”
Jesus said, “I came into the world for this reason.”
Jesus said, “I came to testify to the truth.”
Jesus said, “Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος Οὐκοῦν βασιλεὺς εἶ σύ Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς Σὺ λέγεις ὅτι βασιλεύς εἰμι ἐγὼ εἰς τοῦτο γεγέννημαι καὶ εἰς τοῦτο ἐλήλυθα εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἵνα μαρτυρήσω τῇ ἀληθείᾳ πᾶς ὁ ὢν ἐκ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀκούει μου τῆς φωνῆς

passages.text: “What is truth?” Pilate asked. And having said this, he went out again to the Jews and told them, “I find no basis for a charge against Him.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate asked, “What is truth?”
After Pilate said this, he left Jesus.
Pilate went out to the Jewish leaders.
Pilate spoke to the Jews.
Pilate said, “I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος Τί ἐστιν ἀλήθεια Καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν πάλιν ἐξῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ οὐδεμίαν εὑρίσκω ἐν αὐτῷ αἰτίαν

passages.text: But it is your custom that I release to you one prisoner at the Passover. So then, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
passages.sermon:
Pilate spoke to the people.
Pilate was the Roman governor.
He knew the Jewish custom at Passover.
This custom allowed one prisoner to be released.
Pilate said, "It is your custom that I release one prisoner to you at Passover."
Pilate asked, "Do you want me to release the King of the Jews to you?"
passages.original: ἔστιν δὲ συνήθεια ὑμῖν ἵνα ἕνα ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν ἐν τῷ πάσχα βούλεσθε οὖν ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν Βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: “Not this man,” they shouted, “but Barabbas!” (Now Barabbas was an insurrectionist.)
passages.sermon:
The crowd shouted loudly.
They said, “Not this man.”
They meant Jesus.
They said, “But Barabbas!”
Barabbas was an insurrectionist.
passages.original: Ἐκραύγασαν οὖν πάλιν λέγοντες Μὴ τοῦτον ἀλλὰ τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἦν δὲ ὁ Βαραββᾶς λῃστής
